questions.text: I often worry that my partner will stop loving me
I need a lot of reassurance that I am loved
I get upset when my partner is around less than I'd like
I am afraid of being abandoned
I think a lot about our relationship
I feel uncomfortable opening up to my partner completely
I prefer not to depend on others
I find it hard to ask for support
I keep my distance when things get too close
I find it easier to deal with problems on my own

results.name: Secure
results.body: You can be close without losing yourself, and alone without feeling abandoned. You trust, you communicate, and you don't play games — because you don't need to. It sounds simple, but it's rare, and it makes you the person others feel safe with.
results.youGrowWhen: you keep choosing partners who can meet you where you are.

results.name: Anxious
results.tagline: You love with your whole heart.
results.body: When you care, you care completely — and a part of you quietly fears losing it. You're deeply attuned to the people you love, sometimes so much that their moods become yours. Your capacity for closeness is a gift; it just needs a calmer inner anchor.
results.youGrowWhen: you build security inside yourself, not only in others.

results.name: Avoidant
results.body: You value your freedom and handle life on your own terms — asking for help doesn't come naturally. Closeness can feel like pressure, so you keep a little distance to breathe. Underneath the self-reliance is more warmth than you let show.
results.youGrowWhen: you let the right people in and lean on them a little.

results.name: Fearful
results.body: You crave deep connection and fear it at the same time — pulled in, then pulling back. It's not confusion; it's a heart that has learned to be careful. When you feel truly safe, few people love as fully as you do.
results.youGrowWhen: you build trust slowly, in small, safe steps.
